items.summary_html: Cloudflare replaced full DNS zone rebuilds with a planner that selects the smallest provably safe update and a scheduler that combines work for the same zone. The changes cut peak memory by 85% and halved the delay from a DNS change to its data being written to Quicksilver without rebuilding tens of millions of records for a settings change.
items.title: How we halved DNS build delay and cut memory use by 85% (18 minute read)

items.summary_html: Hidden import chains often load heavy code upfront that teams thought they had deferred, which slows page loads. Next.js 16.4 adds an agent skill that reads Turbopack's module graph, finds these problems, and can apply the fixes, plus new Bundle Analyzer views for route sizes, snapshot diffs, and the critical render path. At Vercel, it removed nearly 2 MB of compressed JavaScript across v0 and vercel.com, so Turbopack users can get similar savings with little manual work.
items.title: Ship less JavaScript in Next.js with your AI agent (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Maple moved its observability app from React to Foldkit using about 40 Claude agents, with most human effort going into a harness that compared more than 2,600 screen variants across pixels, structure, network requests, and accessibility. The rewrite took three days, but code review still found about 180 defects the screenshots missed, and the startup bundle roughly doubled.
items.title: Porting 287,000 lines of React in 3 days. The hard part was proving nothing changed. (11 minute read)

items.summary_html: Coding interviews no longer predict success when AI can outperform candidates on the same tasks, according to this hiring perspective. Newer engineers can stand out by tying their work to business goals, choosing one bold idea, and proving it with a weekend prototype.
items.title: Hunger beats tenure: Advice for junior engineers (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: AI makes it cheap to generate changes, but understanding, reviewing, and coordinating them still consumes the same limited human attention. Clearer intent about priorities and scope, plus a deliberate gate between experiments and the shared product, can help teams keep control of their direction.
items.title: Our organizations are being DDoSed from the inside (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: A single week brought a pile-up of major security failures: a certificate authority issued keys that were trivially guessable numbers, critical flaws hit PHP, GitLab, and Node.js, Railway leaked customer secrets, and PingCAP's TiDB control plane was breached for a month. AI now makes vulnerabilities faster to find and easier to exploit, even for nontechnical attackers. Teams will likely need automated patching, constant security monitoring, and AI-driven defense, and security will cost more.
items.title: Time to rethink software security because of AI? (10 minute read)

items.summary_html: AiSOC is a self-hostable security operations platform that combines alerts, uses LLM agents for triage, and supports investigations mapped to MITRE ATT&CK. A replayable decision ledger records agent steps, and an MCP server exposes the system to connected coding assistants.
items.title: AiSOC (GitHub Repo)

items.summary_html: Disc Image Studio turns images into data patterns that become visible artwork on the recording surface of CDs, DVDs, and single-layer Blu-ray discs. Windows supports design and burning, while experimental Linux and macOS command-line builds generate disc images offline.
items.title: Disc Image Studio (GitHub Repo)

items.summary_html: CheerpJ brings Java 21 and preview support for Java 25 to the browser, with a full OpenJDK that can compile as well as run Java applications. Its new WasmGC engine is experimental and opt-in, with production readiness planned for CheerpJ 6.0.
items.title: CheerpJ 5.0 (10 minute read)

items.summary_html: Doop is a multiplayer design canvas where people and AI agents edit together through a built-in MCP server. It supports live cursors, threaded comments, clickable prototypes, and self-hosting with embedded Postgres for local development.
items.title: Doop (GitHub Repo)

items.summary_html: Explore central Warsaw as an interactive 3D voxel map built from GUGiK and OpenStreetMap data. Controls for date, time, and weather let you change the scene's lighting and atmosphere, and the source code is available to inspect.
items.title: Warsaw in voxels (Website)

items.summary_html: Ai2's benchmark, built from ICLR 2026 peer reviews, tests whether LLMs can judge research novelty and finds that small prompt changes can swing accuracy by more than 50 points on AI-generated ideas. Extra retrieval and reasoning did not reliably help, so teams using LLM judges should test their stability on the kinds of ideas they plan to score.
items.title: Can we trust LLMs to judge whether a research idea is novel? (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: Smarsh turned the AWS Agentic AI Lens into a Claude skill that checks all 150 best practices against a GitHub repository and produces an evidence-cited workbook in hours. The review surfaced gaps such as missing prompt-injection screening and cost controls, making follow-up architecture discussions more focused.
items.title: Automating agentic AI Well-Architected reviews with the AWS Agentic AI Lens (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: This experimental compiler turns TypeScript and JavaScript into native executables or WebAssembly.
items.title: scriptc (GitHub Repo)

items.summary_html: ScanRuler measures 3D scans, compares them against CAD models, and maps wall thickness entirely in the browser.
items.title: ScanRuler (GitHub Repo)

items.summary_html: The Express team patched denial-of-service flaws in body-parser and multer and recommends updating Node.js for the separate upstream Brotli decoder vulnerability.
items.title: October 2026 Express security releases (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Leaflet's first 2.0 beta adds tree-shaking, bundled TypeScript types, and accessibility improvements, reducing a map with a tile layer from 38 kB to 25.6 kB gzipped while introducing breaking API changes.
items.title: Leaflet 2.0 beta (Website)

items.summary_html: GPT-6.2-Astra has started appearing in Codex usage breakdowns. The requests are likely being quietly routed to the new model as part of an A/B test or a staged rollout. A public launch could be days away. OpenAI reportedly decided to skip GPT-6.1 Astra due to concerns about deception and scope.
items.title: GPT-6.2 Astra appears in Codex usage ahead of possible launch (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Anthropic disclosed in its updated IPO filing that it may soon reach its internal definition of recursive self-improvement (RSI), where AI systems help develop increasingly capable AI models.
items.title: Anthropic Warns It May Be Close to Self-Improving AI (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Anthropic released message threads in public beta, allowing agents to send only new messages instead of resending their entire conversation history. The feature reduced median time to first token by approximately 35% for requests with 500K–1M tokens, without changing token usage.
items.title: Claude Introduces Message Threads (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Swarms are AI systems where multiple agents cooperate towards a shared goal. This post discusses a technique called collective inference-time scaling, where agents scale the amount of useful work performed in parallel and the communication needed to achieve it. It also explains how to design incentives for parallel work, and covers the general topic of designing incentives for reinforcement learning.
items.title: How to Train a Swarm (19 minute read)

items.summary_html: Microsoft's Copilot Cowork, an AI-driven agentic execution layer, achieved global availability in four and a half months, switching its runtime from Python to Rust while live. Key practices included writing clear specs before coding, running narrow agents with clear boundaries, and ensuring automated checks genuinely verify code changes. The transition to Rust improved efficiency and highlighted the importance of clear testing, boundary setting, and human oversight in the development process.
items.title: Lessons from building Copilot Cowork (21 minute read)

items.summary_html: Being able to train reliably on multiple smaller clusters widens the usable training pool for frontier training. A single run could mix accelerator generations and vendors as each island runs on its own schedule. Older generations or less common chips could also participate in a frontier run. One risk with this model is that integrity and safety may become harder when models are trained across providers, as one faulty or compromised site can quietly degrade or tamper with models in ways that are harder to trace.
items.title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to Training on Compute Islands (18 minute read)

items.summary_html: GPU-accelerated Weight Teleportation optimizes RL training by improving weight syncing between trainers and samplers, reducing pause times to under 0.23 seconds. This is achieved using a co-designed compression/decompression pipeline with GPU-accelerated parallel processing, utilizing efficient codecs like LZ4 and Snappy, combined with a Zstd layer.
items.title: GPU-accelerated Weight Teleportation (17 minute read)

items.summary_html: Framer's Harness 2 significantly upgrades the agent's execution process, allowing entire workflows in one program, achieving up to 33% cost reduction and 20% faster execution. This is done by executing JavaScript as it streams in, avoiding multiple model calls and using eager execution and early cancellation to enhance efficiency. The redesign also replaces DSL with method calls for real-time updates, making task execution streamlined for both in-app and external agents, reducing tool steps by 43% and cached input tokens by 39% per message.
items.title: Harness 2: executing agent code as it streams (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: NVIDIA introduced new Cosmos Framework capabilities for training, fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, and optimizing world models for physical AI. Developers can generate synchronized video and LiDAR simulations for robotics and autonomous vehicles, then deploy models through GPU-accelerated Cosmos NIM microservices.
items.title: NVIDIA's Cosmos Framework (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenAI plans to merge the Chat and Work tabs within the ChatGPT experience after an initial testing period with select users. Codex will remain a separate experience in the ChatGPT desktop app. The change will enable users to move from exploring ideas to having the chatbot complete work within the same space. Users can import files and plugins. Both ChatGPT and Codex will soon draw from the same allowance pool.
items.title: OpenAI is finally merging ChatGPT's Chat and Work tabs (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: A recent paper demonstrates GPT-6 Astra's ability to interact with neural network weights directly, surpassing human or conventional algorithm capabilities. Astra significantly improved a 0.8B Qwen LLM's mathematical skills by editing weights natively. While impressive, these capabilities reflect advanced problem-solving akin to skilled human researchers, not radically new AI capabilities.
items.title: LLMs are not superhuman at reading and writing neural network weights (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Anthropic's amended IPO prospectus reveals a 1,200% increase in revenue to $33.24 billion for the first nine months of 2026. The company reported a net loss of $104 billion for the same period. Anthropic's commitments for compute and infrastructure total approximately $895.4 billion.
items.title: Anthropic releases amended IPO prospectus with third-quarter financials (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: Enclaves are a new security primitive for cross-repository GitHub Agentic Workflows that lets agents work on different repositories while limiting what they say to each other.
items.title: Limit what agents learn about private repos with enclaves (17 minute read)

items.summary_html: LifeVal is a benchmark designed to evaluate AI performance on practical everyday tasks such as budgeting, finding childcare, and accessing government services.
items.title: OpenAI Introduces LifeVal to Measure AI Performance on Everyday Tasks (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Elon Musk confirmed that Grok Bot usage limits were reduced after operating costs became unsustainably high relative to revenue.
items.title: Elon Musk Limits Grok Bot Usage Over Rising Costs (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: The research extends Anthropic's "Teaching Claude Why" methods to new models, focusing on reducing agentic misalignment through synthetic document finetuning (SDF) and supervised finetuning (SFT) with fictional stories and ethical dilemmas.
items.title: Teaching Qwen Why (47 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenAI added 200 million users over just the past two months. Its growth is accelerating. ChatGPT's search volume is approximately 20% of Google's, and its users create 1.5 billion images with it per week. This post contains an edited transcript of an interview with ChatGPT consumer product lead Adam Fry, where he discusses OpenAI's plans to merge ChatGPT's Chat and Work modes, image generation, interactive interfaces, advertising, education, and public unease about AI.
items.title: OpenAI: ChatGPT Search Is About 20% of Google's, 250 Million People Speak With ChatGPT, and Chat Is Merging With Work (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Developers can now enable their apps to bring content and actions directly into Siri AI by using App Intents. Skills are available for more complex requests that require Siri to combine several actions into a single experience. Siri AI can now surface any entity in the Spotlight semantic index. Submissions to the App Store for apps with the new capabilities will open up in the spring.
items.title: Siri AI is now open to all developers (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: The fringe movement of biohackers and people taking a more hands-on approach to longevity has moved into the mainstream thanks to the COVID-19 pandemic and AI chatbots. More and more people are now taking their health into their own hands and spending time, money, and energy on health and longevity. This post looks at how people view health and explores how the people at the cutting edge of health and technology approach their own health. Some of the biggest opportunities in longevity will go to the companies that help people take action and manage their health over time.
items.title: The State of Longevity (18 minute read)

items.summary_html: BrainCo, a Chinese neurotech company, is developing a wearable device that suppresses appetite by stimulating the brain. It aims to bring the device to market within the next two to three years. The device will launch first in China before potentially expanding to the US. BrainCo currently markets brain-computer interface-enabled headsets to address neurological disorders such as autism, ADHD, and insomnia. Its devices can collect, decode, and stimulate neural signals.
items.title: Neuralink's China Rival Targets Obesity With ‘Electronic' GLP-1 (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: AI-native startups can ship even faster than fast-moving pre-AI startups because they risk nothing by moving too fast. The old constraints of software engineering have disappeared, allowing startups to move faster, but also break things. The new constraints are too much context switching, losing shared context, tougher pacing, less focus on design, and AI plan limits. Many existing technologies and processes will crack under the change.
items.title: How software engineering is changing: a tale of two eras (32 minute read)

items.summary_html: Interpolative software is code that is solidly within the training distribution of models. It can often be specified with just a few sentences of prompting. Novel software is something that has fundamentally not existed before. Writing novel software with agents is challenging, as they are not trained on the task. Not a lot of software is novel, which is fine, as there is still a ton of value in the interpolative stuff.
items.title: Interpolative Software (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: The economics of angel investing have shifted. Many investors have realized it's potentially more profitable to raise a fund instead of using their own money. Technology startups now move much faster, and running around grabbing small checks from angels is less palatable than grabbing a pre-seed fund to fund a whole initial round. Also, when angels try to fund a round, they are often pushed out by the valuation game.
items.title: The Death of the Angel Investor (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: Google will turn off AI tools in its software for K-12 students unless school administrators explicitly choose to make them available. However, schools that choose to restrict AI entirely will also lose access to Google search. Google had earlier turned on AI features as the default option and is claiming that the reversal is in response to feedback from educators and parents. The company's decision to use this strategy shows how much power it has over the US education system.
items.title: Google Will Turn Off Search for Schools That Reject AI (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: This post looks at how Namespace builds custom Mac racks, how it starts macOS instances from scratch in seconds, and how to deliver new Xcode versions mere hours after Apple releases them.
items.title: Mac at any scale (14 minute read)

items.summary_html: A look at how jobs in software have evolved from the 1940s to now.
items.title: A Family Tree of Software Job Titles (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: Adaptive Dark Mode in Safari adapts light websites and presents them as dark.
items.title: Introducing Adaptive Dark Mode (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: Revenue at the median SaaS company grew 0.20% in September, then shrank 0.41% the month after.
items.title: The SaaS apocalypse started in October (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: Revolut runs GLM-5.3 on 56 Nvidia B200 GPUs.
items.title: British fintech Revolut slashes AI coding costs 10x by cutting out Claude and going self-hosted (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: It appears that the cost of running servers is significantly cheaper than what providers are charging, assuming high capacity.
items.title: How much do tokens really cost? (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: A Renault's clock settings were inaccessible without a legitimate navigation SD card, turning a daylight-saving adjustment into a firmware reverse-engineering project. QEMU emulation exposed how a script parser's file writes and Linux's core-dump handling could combine into code execution. The eventual fix changed the stored GPS time offset from 180 minutes to 120.
items.title: Jailbreaking my car's navigation system just so I can change the time (10 minute read)

items.summary_html: Network-attached storage adds latency inside a database cluster, even when the application and database are close together. Local NVMe avoids that hop, but requires deliberate replication and failover to preserve durability. Workloads that fit mostly in RAM may see little benefit, while frequent cache misses and IOPS limits make storage placement worth examining.
items.title: The hidden latency inside your database (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenAI built Pando, a Git-compatible backend that handles pushes to unrelated branches independently and reuses cached packfiles across fetches. It reduced median push latency by nearly 80% and now serves nearly a petabyte of Git data per day. The tradeoff is weaker consistency across branches and some redundant downloads, allowing writes to scale horizontally and reads to saturate clients' network connections.
items.title: Scaling Git at OpenAI (22 minute read)

items.summary_html: Uncritically accepting agent output can increase technical debt while eroding the understanding needed to debug and maintain a system. Choose how much to delegate based on risk, stay involved in consequential decisions, and ask for small, comprehensible changes. When delegating more fully, use independent observability, deterministic checks, and shadow traffic to verify behavior rather than relying solely on the agent's account.
items.title: Resisting Cognitive Surrender (12 minute read)

items.summary_html: Warner Music Group encourages candidates to use AI while solving realistic API integration problems against a live, randomized test server. Its system-design interview asks candidates to modify an existing system and infer causes from observed behavior. The approach emphasizes technical judgment, although building new coding exercises and training senior system-design interviewers remain costly.
items.title: Auditioning Engineering: Software Engineering Interviews in the Age of AI (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: This critique separates experiments that inspect small networks' raw weights from larger-model experiments that use Python and execution feedback. The Qwen result involved 50 batches of practice problems, so it does not demonstrate improvement from inspecting raw weights alone. The distinction matters when judging whether the work shows one general capability or several different engineering techniques.
items.title: The weight-space programming post is misleading (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: djs is a JavaScript and TypeScript engine written in Rust for agent-generated scripts running in a WebAssembly sandbox. It keeps the entire VM state in one byte array, allowing execution to pause between instructions, snapshot while waiting for tools, and resume elsewhere. The focused runtime deliberately omits features such as ES modules, Intl, and a JIT.
items.title: djs (GitHub Repo)

items.summary_html: Office Engine embeds DOCX, XLSX, and PPTX viewing and editing in a browser through React or a web component. Progressive loading, Web Worker parsing, and virtualized views handle large files, while saves regenerate edited parts and preserve the original bytes elsewhere.
items.title: Office Engine (GitHub Repo)

items.summary_html: Three-Live compiles a declarative subset of Three.js into GLB and USDZ assets for web, Android, and Apple rendering pipelines. It runs generated scripts with execution timeouts and geometry quotas, then hands the assets to platform-specific viewers. The Apache-licensed project is in Developer Preview and is not an officially supported Google product.
items.title: Three-Live (GitHub Repo)

items.summary_html: Experiments show GPT-6 Astra reading and directly editing neural network weights without gradient descent, including writing small game-playing networks from scratch. Editing 0.016% of Qwen3.5-0.8B's weights reduced reasoning loops and raised MATH-500 accuracy from 7.9% to 48.1% with 50 forward passes for feedback. The gains removed an obstacle to existing ability, while similar edits failed to meaningfully improve a Gemma model that rarely looped.
items.title: Sparks of Weight-Space Programming (20 minute read)

items.summary_html: A port of Stockfish running on a 200 MHz Pentium Pro with 64 MB of RAM reaches a measured rating of 3180 at 30 seconds per move. The experiment attributes much of chess engines' progress to better search and evaluation rather than faster hardware. Its roughly 3300 rating at classical time controls is extrapolated from shorter games, and readers can play the machine online.
items.title: Could a modern chess engine on a Pentium have defeated Kasparov in 1996? (15 minute read)

items.summary_html: HackerTV turns videos recommended in Hacker News comments into shared, continuously scheduled TV channels with a retro interface.
items.title: HackerTV (Website)

items.summary_html: Namespace explains the hardware, networking, virtualization, and VM-image distribution work behind running a fleet of Macs for cloud development and CI.
items.title: Mac at any scale (14 minute read)

items.summary_html: Subtle details, footnotes, and Easter eggs in public work can reward close attention and help people with shared interests find each other.
items.title: Curiosity Traps (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: C++26's draft failed its ISO ballot amid objections to Contracts, leaving the committee to agree on a revised path and putting the release schedule in doubt.
items.title: C++26 DIS failed, how does C++ survive? (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: Baseten announced Grid for model routing and governance, resumable VM-isolated Sandboxes for agent execution, and general availability of Loops for serverless supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. The products connect training, inference, and execution, with customers retaining ownership of trained weights.
items.title: Baseten Introduces Grid, Sandboxes, and Serverless Loops (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: Developers can now integrate Siri AI into their apps with the iOS 27.3 beta. This update allows apps to leverage Siri's advanced features, like natural language processing and personal context understanding, enhancing user interaction. Siri AI is currently unavailable in the EU and for users under 13. It supports multiple languages, with more to come.
items.title: Siri AI is now open to all developers (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Fireworks AI unveiled new products at Forge, including Ultra-fast inference reaching up to 1,500 tokens per second, lower-cost background processing, and Nexus for accessing multiple AI models within existing tools. It also introduced capabilities for model evaluation, fine-tuning deployment, and enterprise-controlled infrastructure.
items.title: Fireworks Launches Faster AI Inference and Enterprise Tools (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: Linium is a two-person research lab that is trying to train its own generative video models entirely from scratch, aiming to create tools to democratize access to animation. Pyramid-JiT (P-JiT) is a pixel-space architecture that achieves aggressive token reduction through a noise schedule that helps pixel-space models better learn fine-grained detail. This study looks at how models trained on the architecture perform when trained for longer as a pressure test along the way towards larger models and video. Examples of images generated by the resulting model are available.
items.title: Training a Text-to-Image Model for $21K (13 minute read)

items.summary_html: Lower reasoning effort reduces cost much more than it lowers the quality of results. Tests show that models on low reasoning can match models on high reasoning at lower cost. The impact of reasoning effort depends on the task.
items.title: How Much Does Reasoning Effort Affect Score and Cost? (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: The article outlines issues faced during public evaluations of LLMs and details improvements made to benchmarks such as AUTOMATIONBENCH and OFFICEQA PRO V2. They replaced ambiguous prose descriptions with JSON schemas for better performance evaluations and introduced new grading systems to improve accuracy. A multi-layered monitoring system is suggested to prevent manipulation and ensure accurate measurement of model capabilities.
items.title: Learnings from Auditing Public Evaluations (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: It is almost impossible to verify which model produced a specific output. Cryptographic proofs of inference allow model providers to prove that preach suppose was produced which a specific model. These proofs could enable new applications and contribute to a toolkit for verifying compliance with AI pacing requirements. This post details the progress made on a powerful type of cryptographic proof uniquely fit for provable inference called zKSNARK.
items.title: Progress on provable inference for large language models (30 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenAI is leveraging its AI models to enhance mechanical and electrical engineering processes, from design to simulation and production, speeding up internal workflows and improving industry practices. Engineers utilize models like GPT‑6 Astra for tasks such as device design, CAD model creation, and performance simulations, while collaborating with companies like Mazda to explore applications in vehicle aerodynamics.
items.title: Accelerating engineering for the physical world (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: The Gemini Notebook API is a REST interface for programmatically creating and managing notebooks and sources in Gemini Notebook. It can turn web pages, YouTube videos, plain text, and Markdown into persistent notebooks. The API and MCP server are in an early access Public Preview. Only personal Google Accounts are supported during the preview - Google Workspace accounts are not yet supported.
items.title: Gemini Notebook API (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: ChatGPT's search volume has reached 20% of Google's, with ChatGPT rapidly gaining 200 million users in the past two months, leading to 1.2 billion weekly active users. The voice mode of ChatGPT now engages 250 million weekly active users, emphasizing new interaction methods through GPT Live updates that enable natural bidirectional conversations. Plans to merge Chat and Work modes aim to simplify user interaction, while Dots highlights innovations in AI task management despite high compute costs.
items.title: OpenAI: ChatGPT Search Is About 20% of Google's, 250 Million People Speak With ChatGPT, and Chat Is Merging With Work (16 minute read)

items.summary_html: DeepSeek plans to use Huawei's Ascend AI chips to pretrain DeepSeek V5. Ascend chips have previously been used primarily for inference rather than pretraining. This will be an important test of whether Chinese AI accelerators can support the full pre-training of a frontier large language model. A successful run could reduce Chinese AI developers' dependence on Nvidia hardware and strengthen Huawei's position as an alternative for advanced AI computing.
items.title: DeepSeek Plans to Train Its Next-Generation Model on Huawei Ascend Chips (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: The 'Astra can read and write weights' claims are misleading.
items.title: The 'Astra can read and write weights to improve Qwen' post is misleading (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenAI just merged animated GIF output into its image generation, with the animations being generated by OpenAI's Images API, which means it is coming to ChatGPT.
items.title: ChatGPT is about to start making GIFs (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: This post explains how state machines enforce agent permissions, approvals, retries, and completion criteria outside model prompts.
items.title: Agent State Machines: Building Deterministic Scaffolding for Agents (9 minute read)

items.summary_html: AI tokens' pricing appears sustainable, as competition among providers is driving down costs.
items.title: How much do tokens really cost? (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: Starfall is an uncrewed SpaceX reentry capsule shaped like a disk, about 10 feet across and 2.5 feet tall, that launches on Falcon 9, with Starship planned. It returns up to 1,000 kg from orbit by parachute and ocean splashdown, targeting about 700 nautical miles off the US West Coast. SpaceX's stated goals are fast point-to-point cargo delivery and return of in-space manufactured goods. The first demo launched on June 23, and it puts SpaceX in competition with return-capsule startups like Varda.
items.title: SpaceX's Starfall is a flat disk capsule built to return up to 1,000 kg from orbit (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: On its earnings call, Apple CEO John Ternus called memory pricing “unprecedented” and said costs will rise again in the December quarter and beyond. Apple's manufacturing purchase obligations rose $33 billion in the September quarter, to $89.7 billion, to lock in supply. It guided December gross margin to 45% to 46%, and expects Macs and iPads to stay supply-constrained through the holidays. Apple raised prices on some Macs, iPads, and iPhones earlier this year.
items.title: Apple warns memory costs keep rising, as supplier purchase commitments jump $33B in one quarter (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Qualcomm's first High Bandwidth Compute silicon passed lab validation. HBC bonds stacked LPDDR memory to an AI accelerator base die, so compute sits under the memory and data travels less. Qualcomm claims 18x the effective bandwidth of LPDDR5X and over 5x the bandwidth per watt of HBM4, from early tests. HBC debuts in the Dragonfly AI250 inference accelerator, sampling in the first half of 2027.
items.title: Qualcomm says HBC silicon passes lab validation: 18x LPDDR5X bandwidth, 5x HBM4 bandwidth per watt (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Foxconn wants to turn other companies' quantum designs into production systems, without owning the qubit technology itself. Chairman Young Liu told CNBC he sees the machines as accelerators attached to CPUs and GPUs for hard NP-type problems, not general-purpose computers, and puts commercial viability at least two years out. One cost driver he flagged is cabling: a single cable built for the low-temperature requirements can cost over $1,000.
items.title: Foxconn plans to contract-build other companies' quantum computers, treating them as accelerators next to CPUs and GPUs (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Orbital Matter's Replicator-2 satellite 3D printed a half-meter rigid beam in orbit by extruding coils of resin cured with UV light, a first for a free-flying spacecraft. One of two printers meant to deploy a solar array failed, but the boom the other made did deploy the array. Boom length is limited only by onboard resin, and the company thinks 100 m is feasible. A 2028 mission targets a 5 kW array, then 100+ kW per wing by 2030.
items.title: Orbital Matter prints a half-meter rigid beam in orbit by UV-curing extruded resin (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Intel released 14A PDK 0.9 to outside customers, with PDK 1.0 planned for Q1 2027. A PDK is the set of design rules and transistor models chip designers build against, so 0.9 is where external designs can start taking shape. Intel's schedule still has risk production for its own products in the second half of 2027 and volume production in 2028, and it claims 14A is ahead of 18A on defect density and transistor performance at the same stage.
items.title: Intel's 14A PDK 0.9 goes to outside customers, with PDK 1.0 due in Q1 2027 (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Agility goes public via SPAC at roughly $2.8 billion on $1.8 million of 2025 revenue. Its gross margin was -151%, since a Digit costs about $125,000 to build against a $75,000 target. Unitree is worth about $40 billion on $239 million of revenue and 5,500 humanoids sold, but its gross margin slipped to 54%, and humanoids' margin edge over its other products shrank to 6 points. Agility spends about 4.5x Unitree's R&D on 1/134th of its revenue.
items.title: Agility lists at roughly 1,550x 2025 sales with a -151% gross margin, while Unitree's humanoid margin premium shrinks (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: Northwood Space raised a $375 million Series C at a $2 billion valuation, co-led by a16z and DFJ Growth, alongside a financing agreement with HSBC. Founded in 2022 and led by CEO Bridgit Mendler, it builds antennas and software that help satellites communicate with Earth. It raised a $100 million Series B in January and won a nearly $50 million Space Force contract to upgrade the satellite control network.
items.title: Northwood Space raises $375M at a $2B valuation to scale satellite communications gear (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: Samsung will reportedly use its second Taylor, Texas, foundry to build base dies, the logic layer at the bottom of an HBM stack, for AMD and Nvidia on a 2nm process.
items.title: Samsung to make HBM base dies for AMD and Nvidia on 2nm at a second Texas fab, per Maeil (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Pixel is a low-cost wheeled humanoid with human-aligned kinematics and compliant grippers.
items.title: Pixel co-designs a low-cost wheeled humanoid with its data collection, controller, and policy stack (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Entegris bought Advanced Abrasives, a maker of diamond super-abrasives used to polish hard substrates like SiC, and plans a new SiC CMP line in Taiwan.
items.title: Entegris moves into SiC and diamond thermal materials for AI packaging via an acquisition and an Element Six deal (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Barclays estimates Elon Musk would own about 37% of a potential combined company but hold about 56% of the vote, since his SpaceX shares carry 10x votes.
items.title: Barclays estimates Musk would hold about 56% of the vote in a combined SpaceX-Tesla (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Apple quietly lowered the daily spending cap on AI models for its employees last month. Some engineers had their budgets cut from $300 to $200, and the company is planning further cuts for some engineering teams that may potentially reduce their daily allowances to as little as $100. Groups outside of engineering may have their limits reduced to $25 from $100. Employees say that few workers were using their full $300 daily allowances, making the previous limits unnecessarily generous.
items.title: Apple Cuts Internal AI Usage Budgets in Move to Reduce Spending (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenAI is rolling out Images 2.6 globally in ChatGPT and Codex. The new model generates images 50% faster than the previous iteration, and it can also create GIFs. Users can adjust the speed of GIFs, edit individual frames, and share them. GPT-Image-2.6 Flare and Sunburst are now available through the API.
items.title: OpenAI launches Images 2.6 with GIFs and image reference (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: SpaceX has launched a commercial page for Starfall, a disk-shaped reentry capsule that can carry up to 1,000 kg of payload. The capsule can supply 1 kW of power and connect to the internet through Starlink, allowing researchers to pull data from experiments while in orbit instead of waiting for splashdown. It can be used for manufacturing, research, or testing and is aimed at biomedical customers, pharmaceutical companies, and materials science research. Starfall's timeline will depend on Starship - SpaceX is preparing for Flight 15, where it aims to catch both stages with the launch tower.
items.title: SpaceX's Starfall just went from secret to storefront (16 minute read)

items.summary_html: Varda Space Industries' autonomous factories carry miniature laboratories in which materials can be processed without astronauts. Once the process is complete, a capsule separates from the spacecraft and returns to Earth. The company currently has three spacecraft simultaneously in orbit. Manufacturing in space has several advantages, one of the most important being microgravity. Varda plans to launch seven missions in 2027 and 10 in 2028.
items.title: Why pharma firms are going to Earth's orbit in search of new cancer drugs (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: Design engineering requires being deeply involved in the technical craft and material of software. They help make decisions about functionality and architecture in code while still being a designer. Design engineers are uniquely positioned to make convincing prototypes of future theories. They are the perfect people to help figure out the shape of the future.
items.title: Fortune Telling and Speculative Design (21 minute read)

items.summary_html: The new version of X.com's web app was built by five engineers working with AI coding agents in under six months. It loads pages significantly faster than the old web app over slow connections, and it already serves logged-out users and the pages that search engines crawl. This post covers why X.com was rebuilt, how the new web app is being rolled out, and how the old and new apps compare today. It also looks at the performance work completed since logged-out traffic moved over.
items.title: Rebuilding the global town square from scratch (32 minute read)

items.summary_html: Voice is a natural modality that is underutilized. It is great for rambling at coding agents and for capturing context. There is a lot of ambient context that exists in conversations with a ton of downstream value. This post presents some use cases for voice as a way to interact with AI.
items.title: Voice is Underutilized (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: Nearly every relevant local ballot measure opposing data centers won or is winning, with the exception of North Dakota. The constraint on AI dispersion is becoming political. AI will likely be a scarcity for much longer than expected. This post looks at what the implications might be if Americans don't change their minds about data centers.
items.title: AI on the Ballot (18 minute read)

items.summary_html: Adoption across all other firms is still rising.
items.title: The Top 1% of AI Spenders Stalled in Q3. So Did Anthropic's Dollar Growth (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: US AI capacity will grow from 38 GW today to an 81 GW ceiling in 2027.
items.title: Watts in Store for 2027: The AI Ceiling (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: Teams need to be more selective about which bugs to focus on fixing, as it isn't practical nowadays to fix everything.
items.title: Bug Finding Considered Harmful? (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: Agents make ads businesses less effective, but agentic spending is an opportunity to make up for any revenue shortfall.
items.title: Payments are the new ads (12 minute read)

items.summary_html: Sequoia Capital is closing its London office, shutting down its Arc accelerator and its Scouts program, merging its early-stage and growth teams into one, flattening its partnership, and killing the Monday partner meeting.
items.title: Sequoia hits rewind, undoing 20 years of expansion (9 minute read)

items.summary_html: Tamba could be an experimental testing ground for social features rather than a finished product.
items.title: YouTube is cooking up something new called 'Tamba,' and it looks pretty social (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenAI's autonomous security pipeline reproduced 1,724 Linux kernel vulnerabilities and generated exploits for 948 distinct local privilege escalation flaws at an API cost of $1.2 million. Agents handled discovery, runtime validation, exploit development, and candidate patches before human review and maintainer reporting. The research highlights why validation must check how an exploit succeeds, after some agents gained root through a different vulnerability than the one assigned.
items.title: A thousand fewer paths to root (20 minute read)

items.summary_html: Microsoft reduced clarity.js by 1,257 gzip bytes through more than 50 automated change, build, measure, and test experiments. Named imports and minifier settings delivered savings, while extracting small helpers sometimes increased compressed size. A larger saving from modern JavaScript output could not ship because native async functions would break Angular sites that depend on Zone.js.
items.title: How We Made clarity.js 4.5% Smaller Without Sacrificing Compatibility (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: Fast, cheap coding agents can create substantial review work by deleting unrelated code, missing requirements, and making tests pass without exercising the intended behavior. More than 100 hours with Cursor's Composer 2.5 exposed failures ranging from unsolicited edits to disabled schema validation and tests that bypassed API routes. Explicit rules and reference implementations did not reliably prevent repeated mistakes.
items.title: You'll need nerves of steel to work with AI agents (10 minute read)

items.summary_html: Agent systems accumulate debt when prompts and agent loops take responsibility for approvals, side-effect retries, and audit trails. A supplier invoice dispute illustrates how to divide ownership among the model, harness, durable execution, and an orchestration control plane. A single agent inside one application may need only its harness, while processes crossing systems need explicit ownership of recovery and approval.
items.title: Agentic Technical Debt and Where Orchestration Belongs in AI Agent Architecture (9 minute read)

items.summary_html: An account of adopting coding agents at Intento traces the shift from small experiments to a team that delegates code generation and reviews the output. The key change was making documentation, architectural decisions, tasks, and production logs accessible to models. Earlier failures on an established codebase were attributed to missing context that lived in people's heads, rather than the age of the code itself.
items.title: Nobody here writes code by hand anymore (12 minute read)

items.summary_html: Graphify turns code and supporting material into a queryable knowledge graph with paths between concepts and an interactive browser view. Code parsing uses local tree-sitter analysis without an LLM or vector store, while document and media interpretation can use a model. Edges distinguish explicit source relationships from inferred connections, making the graph's evidence easier to inspect.
items.title: Graphify (GitHub Repo)

items.summary_html: This agent skill and dependency-free Node CLI control Chrome directly through the Chrome DevTools Protocol. It supports accessibility snapshots, tab management, screenshots, and raw protocol calls without requiring a separate browser MCP server. Screenshots are written to files so agents can choose when to load them into context.
items.title: faster-chrome-devtools-skill (GitHub Repo)

items.summary_html: Go 1.27 makes encoding/json/v2 and encoding/json/jsontext generally available, addressing behavior and performance constraints that could not be fixed within the old API. The new defaults reject invalid UTF-8 and duplicate object names, while the packages separate Go value conversion from lower-level JSON syntax processing.
items.title: A new Go API for JSON (9 minute read)

items.summary_html: This interactive study compares the original DOOM source with 43 descendants to explore what survives copying, porting, and translation. Structural fingerprints and call relationships can reveal ancestry even when names or source text change. In a blind test, a Go translation's functions were assigned to the correct game subsystem 60% of the time, compared with 20% for shuffled labels.
items.title: DOOM's DNA (Website)

items.summary_html: AI-assisted researchers turned a PHP crash bug reported in 2024 into a critical vulnerability capable of running arbitrary code on a server. Finding the exploit took two weeks, while four engineers spent two months developing a patch, illustrating the growing gap between discovering flaws and safely fixing them. Better funding for open-source maintainers, defensive AI tools, and formal verification could help close that gap.
items.title: The PHP2Shell Vulnerability Heralds Cybersecurity Hell (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenAI's Images 2.6 brings 50% faster image generation, GIF creation, and better consistency across edits.
items.title: Introducing Images 2.6 (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Ricursive released Ripple-65B Preview, a dense open-weight model with up to 1M tokens of context that reports an 80.52 score on TerminalBench 2.1 and a total development and training cost of $32 million.
items.title: Introducing Ripple-65B Preview (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: Parcel 3 rewrites the bundler in Rust and reports cold builds up to 100 times faster than v2.
items.title: Announcing Parcel 3 alpha (11 minute read)

items.summary_html: Anthropic's public-beta message threads let active agents send only new messages each turn, reducing median time to first token by about 35% for requests with 500k to 1M tokens while leaving token usage unchanged.
items.title: Make long-running agents faster with message threads (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenAI is rolling out Images 2.6 globally in ChatGPT and Codex. The new model generates images 50% faster than the previous iteration, and it can also create GIFs. Users can adjust the speed of the GIF, edit individual frames, and share it. GPT-Image-2.6 Flare and Sunburst are now available through the API.
items.title: OpenAI launches Images 2.6 with GIFs and image reference (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: Ripple-65B Preview is a frontier open-weight model that achieves state-of-the-art performance on TerminalBench 2.1. It surpasses significantly larger open-weight models from the US, including Reflection Beam 501B, Meta Muse Spark Open 816B, Thinking Machines Inkling 975B, and Nvidia Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B. The model was trained for only $32 million, one-tenth the estimated cost of the previous open-weight SOTA on agentic coding. Ripple-65B Preview is available on Hugging Face, Together AI, GMI Cloud, and OpenRouter.
items.title: Ripple-65B Preview (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Pangram Image 1.0 is an AI image and AI video detection model that can produce a heatmap localizing exactly where AI appears in images. It is robust to edits, compression, and low resolutions. There is a Chrome Extension available that can detect AI, as well as API support for images and video.
items.title: Introducing Pangram Image 1.0 (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenAI developed an autonomous pipeline for discovering, exploiting, and patching security vulnerabilities. In a single run, its cybersecurity model validated and generated patches for 948 Linux local privilege escalation vulnerabilities.
items.title: How OpenAI Patched 948 Linux Vulnerabilities (12 minute read)

items.summary_html: Axiom has released a Lean formalization of the entire Stacks Project. The Stacks project is an open-source reference that lays the foundation of modern algebraic geometry. The release is the largest integrated, reusable library of formalized mathematics ever built. It makes the full mathematical development of the Stacks Project available as a single, machine-checked library that researchers and AI agents can import from directly into new formal proofs.
items.title: The Stacks Project, formalized in Lean (13 minute read)

items.summary_html: SWE-2 Flash is a coding model that uses a new mid-training stage before reinforcement learning.
items.title: Cognition Introduces SWE-2 Flash (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Hy4 is a large language model with visual understanding capabilities. Tencent plans to release model weights and system cards for the model in the coming days. The model supports a broad range of tasks that include fine-grained image processing, complex chart analysis, and mathematical visual reasoning. It can interact with both command-line interfaces and GUIs to perform a wide range of work and everyday tasks.
items.title: Tencent Launches Hy4, Joining the Ranks of the World's Leading Open-Source AI Models (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: Cartesia's H-Nets learn directly from raw bytes, matching benchmark performance with substantially less training compute.
items.title: H-Nets Learn Directly From Raw Bytes (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: AlphaEvolve is a Gemini-powered coding agent for designing advanced algorithms. It pairs the creative problem-solving capabilities of Gemini models with automated evaluators that verify answers. The agent has been used to enhance the efficiency of Google's data centers, chip design, and AI training process. This repository contains a minimal implementation of AlphaEvolve along with code and data related to solutions and discoveries it has contributed to.
items.title: AlphaEvolve (GitHub Repo)

items.title: OpenAI to acquire Pierre Computer Company, Inc. (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Conductor is a startup that lets developers run multiple AI coding agents in parallel workspaces.
items.title: Meta Acquires AI Coding Startup Conductor (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: Researchers find that frontier language models perform well with shorter contexts without sacrificing accuracy.
items.title: You don't need long context (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: Together Compiler is a truly continual optimization loop that leverages high-throughput agents to optimize for diverse inference workloads.
items.title: Together Compiler: Continual Compilation for AI inference (9 minute read)

items.title: Web grounding for the Decisions API (7 minute read)

items.title: Kimi-K3.1-Pro (10 minute read)

items.summary_html: Recent election results show that voters are overwhelmingly against the massive build-out of compute capacity that Silicon Valley is pushing. This could rein in AI's rapid growth and become a big problem for the tech companies developing the technology, and could have effects on the wider US economy. Stalling construction could result in dire consequences for tech companies that were already struggling to secure enough compute.
items.title: The Election Day Revolt That Threatens America's AI Boom (11 minute read)

items.summary_html: Major investors planning to participate in Anthropic's IPO, expected to launch the week before Thanksgiving, say the expected $1.5 trillion valuation will likely need to come down. The AI lab was expected to raise up to $100 billion, but is now predicted to raise around $80 billion, leaving it with a valuation closer to $1 trillion. Investors have revolted against AI bets this week as the midterm elections have put several AI skeptics in power, potentially slowing data center development in the US. Anthropic has avoided committing to specific plans for its IPO to maintain optionality.
items.title: Major Investors Are Skeptical Anthropic IPO Can Achieve $1.5 Trillion Valuation (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: Blue Origin has announced two significant upgrades to its New Glenn rocket that reduce the cost of manufacturing the vehicle and expand its capacity for payload delivery. The company aims to eventually launch the vehicle more than 1,000 times a year. It has started test firing a new engine that will eventually replace the BE-4 engine that powers the first stage of New Glenn. The company is also developing a hydrogen-oxygen third stage for the rocket to give it an extra kick.
items.title: Blue Origin says it is building a higher-performing rocket engine at 1/4 the cost (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: A SpudCell is an artificial cell created from lifeless ingredients that can grow, copy its DNA, divide in two, and start its cell cycle all over again. It is still far from a self-sustaining cell that any scientist could manufacture from prepared ingredients, but the technology could eventually make it easier to produce medicines, foods, and other items that could not otherwise be produced with ordinary biology. The researchers working on SpudCell hope that it will eventually be a platform for biotechnology that will allow a simple cell to be engineered in scores of useful ways. SpudCell could potentially be misused, so its researchers are taking security seriously from the start - its DNA and proteins are engineered so that it can only survive on an exotic diet of chemicals not found in nature.
items.title: They Created a Cell That's Almost Alive. What to Do With It Now? (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: *sshole is a vulnerability in Linux that allows attackers to log in via SSH without knowing the password. The vulnerability exists in systems using OpenSSH with musl without pluggable authentication modules. Despite the prerequisites, the vulnerabilities likely threaten a large number of systems. It is still unclear where the vulnerability resides and what other packages may be vulnerable.
items.title: Meet *sshole, the vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: GitHub's new Git storage architecture is capable of handling thousands of writes per second with reads that scale on demand. It can support 5,000 concurrent agents working on a repository while serving read traffic with consistently low latency. The new architecture is designed to support agentic development for hundreds of millions of developers. This post walks through the requirements behind the design of the new architecture and explores two of its components.
items.title: Inside GitHub's new Git storage architecture (21 minute read)

items.summary_html: At the heart of Dario Amodei's worldview are two interwoven philosophies: rationalism, which aims to apply dispassionate thinking to the world, and effective altruism, which seeks to maximize social good with mathematical precision. These schools of thought form the foundation for Anthropic. As the company has grown, Amodei's views have become increasingly prominent. This article takes a look at how Anthropic's chief executive's thinking on AI was shaped.
items.title: The Making of Dario Amodei (20 minute read)

items.summary_html: A 'Hackintosh' is a non-Apple computer running macOS. The Hackintosh community started fading away after Apple released its first ARM-based Mac and discontinued support for x86 versions of macOS. However, the rise of AI has revived activity in the space, and there has been an explosion in development, activity, and success in the past few weeks. This post lists a few recent developments, including macOS 27 running on a Snapdragon laptop, iOS 17 running on the Nintendo Switch OLED, and macOS 27.2 Beta on an ARM SBC RK3588 with Mali drivers.
items.title: The Hackintosh Reborn... with AI (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: The average time from disclosure to attack has been falling for some time, but AI has changed who can operate inside that window, and how fast known bugs get weaponized.
items.title: The Exploit Was the Bottleneck (24 minute read)

items.summary_html: Tech companies track, store, and sell a lot of information - they should use it to make the user experience better.
items.title: I wish tech companies knew more about me (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: There will be 100 times more programmers in the next few years, but most of them won't call themselves programmers.
items.title: 100x more programmers (17 minute read)

items.summary_html: Two pieces of common software engineering dogma - avoid global variables and use a database for state - are partially inconsistent.
items.title: A database is a store for global variables (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: This essay looks at what it takes to build a physical platform capable of performing biological experiments, measuring their outcomes reliably, and generating evidence at the scale AI requires.
items.title: Getting Data to Grow in a Dish (30 minute read)

items.summary_html: Elon Musk wants to combine SpaceX's Starlink satellite broadband network with mobile antennas, fiber connections, and other ground infrastructure, so that regular smartphones can seamlessly tap into signals from both Earth and space.
items.title: How Musk Plans to Shake Up the US Wireless Industry (9 minute read)

items.summary_html: Airbnb fine-tuned a model with 2 billion effective parameters to match frontier models on a production policy classifier, reaching 0.902 F1 with 35 ms median latency. At thousands of requests per minute, serving it on one GPU cost roughly 1% as much as frontier APIs, though hosted models were cheaper at low traffic.
items.title: Frontier Quality at 1% of the Cost: A Production Benchmark of LLM Classifiers (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: Tab Widgets traced slow startup to React's 300 ms Suspense reveal throttle, even though its widget code had loaded within about 100 ms. Rendering placeholders without suspending brought the first widget content onscreen about 240 ms sooner in its Windows Chrome tests, while shrinking the startup bundle made no measurable difference.
items.title: React.lazy, Suspense and the Hidden 300 ms Delay (12 minute read)

items.summary_html: GitHub's Rubicon architecture separates immutable Git objects in Azure Blob Storage from reference updates in a dedicated replicated log, letting compute, storage, and maintenance scale independently. Internal tests supported 5,000 concurrent agents and 7,200 pushes per second to one repository, with disposable virtual replicas serving requests and separate workers compacting packs.
items.title: Inside GitHub's New Git Storage Architecture (16 minute read)

items.summary_html: Similar-looking workflows can have different failure modes, audit requirements, and owners, so combining them too early creates flags and coordination costs. Wait until a pattern appears three times for the same reason before extracting it, while sharing stable primitives, design tokens, accessibility behavior, and standards-driven utilities from the start.
items.title: Don't Build the Reusable Component Yet (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: Tests of ten design systems show why interaction performance needs the same attention as accessibility, using a 249-country dropdown and a list of 100 checkboxes as realistic stress cases. The practical approach combines Playwright performance budgets, checks for long frames and nonlinear scaling, and defaults such as automatic virtualization so every app benefits.
items.title: Design Systems Should Be Fast by Default (18 minute read)

items.summary_html: File Viewer previews more than 275 file formats in the browser, including Office documents, PDF, CAD, 3D files, and archives. Its built-in renderers work without a conversion server, with integrations for Vue, React, Svelte, and Web Components and support for self-hosting workers, WASM, and fonts.
items.title: File Viewer (GitHub Repo)

items.summary_html: sidebearing-trim aligns text columns by visible letter shapes rather than glyph box origins. It reads OpenType glyph metrics and applies a negative offset at the start of the line to compensate for the first glyph's sidebearing.
items.title: sidebearing-trim (Website)

items.summary_html: GG Coder is a desktop coding agent that works with existing AI subscriptions, API keys, or local models, with local search of open-source code and an autopilot that continues through verification. The repository also exposes reusable packages for provider connections, tool-using agents, model selection, and coding sessions under an AGPL-3.0 license.
items.title: GG Coder (GitHub Repo)

items.summary_html: Purrkour went from first commit to App Store-ready in three days using a shared TypeScript engine, Expo, and TypeGPU, with procedural graphics and audio. A solver verifies the puzzles, while an AI agent tests actual gameplay through Argent using a debug bridge that exposes board state and exact tap coordinates.
items.title: A WebGPU Cat Puzzle Game Shipped in Three Days on Expo, with an AI Agent as the QA Team (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: NVIDIA uses specialized agents to correlate failures across GPU cluster hardware, networking, scheduling, and observability through one chat interface. The system can run on-premises with local Nemotron models, while read-only Kubernetes credentials, per-session sandboxes, and auditable recommendations give SREs control over investigations.
items.title: How NVIDIA Uses AI Agents to Streamline AI Factory Operations (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: Discord plans to replace Electron on desktop and React Native on mobile with shared Rust app code, while retaining native mobile interfaces. A preview Windows client used 290 MB of RAM, but there is no announced release date and user testing is still planned.
items.title: Discord Is Ditching Electron and Its New App Uses Less RAM (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Splitting common letters across webfont files increases text layout work and interaction latency, which can be reduced by keeping basic Latin together, avoiding overlapping unicode-range declarations, and placing Arabic fonts first on Arabic pages.
items.title: How a Split Webfont Slowed Down My Text Layout, and How I Fixed It (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: Thinking Machines' new mixture-of-experts model has 594B total parameters and 17B active, supports image input and adjustable reasoning effort, and launches on Tinker with Apache 2.0 weights planned for next week after external safety testing.
items.title: Introducing Inkling 2 Small (12 minute read)

items.summary_html: A password authentication bypass in OpenSSH on musl systems without PAM can let specially configured accounts accept long passwords because musl's crypt() failure marker matches the account's stored password field.
items.title: *sshole (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: Despite extensive tracking, tech services still recommend products people already own, ignore explicit language preferences, and miss years of consistent behavior, raising the question of why collected data so rarely improves the experience.
items.title: I Wish Tech Companies Knew More About Me (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenAI introduced GPT-6 Cyber, a cybersecurity model designed to identify and validate exploitable vulnerabilities while staying within researcher-defined boundaries.
items.title: GPT-6 Cyber (13 minute read)

items.summary_html: Inkling 2 Small is a Mixture-of-Experts model with 594B total parameters, 17B active, that supports image inputs and variable effort. The model's vision and agentic capabilities enable it to incorporate visual feedback to iteratively build and refine websites, games, and 3D designs with interactive elements. It will be initially available through Tinker with closed weights. Full weights will be available under an Apache 2.0 license next week after the completion of external safety testing and red-teaming.
items.title: Introducing Inkling 2 Small (37 minute read)

items.summary_html: Google introduces Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, enhancing speed, cost-efficiency, and extended clip lengths for AI models. This update aims to improve developer tools and effectiveness in AI applications.
items.title: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: Anthropic's AI R&D capabilities accelerated significantly, improving model performance on well-defined tasks at roughly twice the rate compared to 2024-2025. This acceleration primarily results from AI's increasing role in R&D, though multiple factors contributed in late 2025.
items.title: Independent Assessment of AI R&D Acceleration at Anthropic in October 2026 (63 minute read)

items.summary_html: Cloudflare has outlined the challenges websites face as AI agents increasingly act on behalf of users, making it harder to verify identities, assess trustworthiness, and assign accountability.
items.title: Cloudflare's Trust Framework for AI Agents (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Blood on the Clocktower is a social deception game. Watching AI play the game unveils a lot about how AI is progressing on a set of AI capabilities that no other benchmark gives clear visibility into. The game requires AI to execute schemes with creativity, on-the-spot bluffing, and collective reasoning. This post looks at what happens when you pit AI models against each other in the game.
items.title: The benchmark where AIs have to lie to win (23 minute read)

items.summary_html: NVIDIA VFlash is a vision model that generates geometric predictions like robot trajectories and 3D motion in parallel rather than token by token.
items.title: NVIDIA Introduced VFlash (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: NVIDIA's Cosmos 3 platform now offers four open-weight models for interactive world simulation and driving scenes, each with 16 billion trainable parameters. These models enable multi-sensor data generation, synchronized observations, and photorealistic video from simulator controls, supporting advanced research in robotics and autonomous driving.
items.title: New NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Open Models for Interactive World Simulation (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: GPU providers sell capacity through reservations, on-demand rentals, and interruptible spot contracts. Reservations help secure financing through predictable revenue, on-demand offers flexibility at higher rates, and spot monetizes idle capacity. Ornn's compute price indices track executed on-demand transactions, excluding reservations and spot rentals.
items.title: How Primary Compute Markets Work (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: Anthropic Personal Finance in Claude allows users to securely connect bank and credit card accounts to ask questions about balances, transactions, and spending.
items.title: Personal Finance in Claude (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Meta announced voice conversations and expressive avatars for its Muse app, allowing users to brainstorm, plan trips, and complete tasks through spoken interactions.
items.title: Muse Voice (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Users just have to describe the tool they want, and Cursor will build it, set up a database, run deterministic and agentic security checks, and deploy.
items.title: You can now build live apps in Cursor and share them with a link (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: Hugging Face released "The Ultimate MoE Training Handbook," a comprehensive guide on training mixture-of-experts models.
items.title: The Ultimate MoE Training Handbook (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: The cost of a Devin Review per PR has dropped by 82% since August.
items.title: Devin Review 2.0 (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: Agility begins trading Thursday after merging with Churchill Capital Corp XI, becoming the first US-listed company focused on humanoid robots. The deal values it at roughly $2.5 billion and expects about $465 million in gross proceeds, including $100 million already received. In 2025, it booked $1.8 million of revenue, over half from five robots bought by one investor, against a $138.1 million net loss. About $38 million of that was non-cash stock compensation, and it burned $99.8 million in cash.
items.title: Agility Robotics lists on Nasdaq as AGLT with $1.8M of revenue and a $138.1M net loss (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Waymo will move rides in Austin and Atlanta to its own app in January 2028, ahead of the Uber deal's May 2028 expiry. Riders on Uber never knew whether they'd get a robotaxi or a human driver. Waymo wants a direct rider relationship.
items.title: Waymo confirms it will leave Uber in Austin and Atlanta in January 2028 (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: Northstar is a methalox booster engine that Blue Origin says cuts mass by 30% and parts count by 50% versus the BE-4 while raising thrust from 640,000 to 715,000 lbf, with assembly in under a day. No first-flight date is given, and New Glenn is still recovering from a pad explosion that happened in May.
items.title: Blue Origin adds a BE-7 third stage to New Glenn and unveils the Northstar engine (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: SpaceX has signed a multiyear deal for Qualcomm's Dragonwing infrastructure platforms: the QRU100 radio unit and QDU100 distributed unit, with 64T64R massive MIMO and physical-layer RAN software. They'll go into base stations at what's planned as tens of thousands of US sites, starting in 2027, to complement Starlink's satellite service. Qualcomm calls this its biggest 5G deal yet.
items.title: Qualcomm to supply MIMO radios and baseband for Starlink Mobile's terrestrial 5G network (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: A Northwestern-led team built FLIP, which makes a physics-based digital twin of the telescope's optics and adjusts it until it reproduces the observed starlight, then subtracts that simulated glare. On existing NIRCam data at 4.3 microns, it improved sensitivity up to 15x over the conventional KLIP method and recovered the giant planet 51 Eridani b, which standard processing couldn't separate from residual glare.
items.title: FLIP software subtracts starlight in JWST coronagraph data with up to 15x better sensitivity (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: LumiTac pairs five photoemitters with five RGBW photoreceivers on opposing circuit boards joined by translucent silicone, so load-driven motion between the layers shifts the internal light field under compression, shear, bending, and torsion. The head is 12 mm across, 4.75 mm thick, under 2 g, and made with about $7 in components. Independent testing gave R² of 0.966 to 0.994, with mean absolute errors of 0.054 to 0.190 N in force and 0.304 to 1.419 mN·m in moment.
items.title: LumiTac is a camera-free six-axis tactile sensor, 12 mm wide and about $7 in parts (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has pledged to halt all data center approvals until the legislature passes new laws when it meets in January. Outgoing Governor Abbott had already paused new grid connections and ordered an audit. Texas holds about 25% of planned US data center capacity. It is estimated that 13.3 GW of announced projects are at risk.
items.title: Texas governor-elect Hinojosa's data center moratorium pledge puts 13.3 GW of announced projects at risk (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: CXMT says its 4F² DRAM uses a vertical surrounding gate transistor and builds the memory cells and peripheral circuitry on separate wafers joined by hybrid bonding, which an analyst says could raise density by about 30%. Yields are unknown, and a server product is promised before year-end. The claim cut Samsung and SK Hynix about 13% in a day, even though CXMT holds roughly 10% of DRAM against Samsung's 38%.
items.title: CXMT's chairman tops China's newcomers at $13B on an unverified claim of a 4F² DRAM breakthrough (3 minute read)

items.title: Shield Space plans swarms of up to 100 laser-armed cubesat interceptors, starting with a 2027 rendezvous demo (4 minute read)

The board says that it has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised. items.title: What to Know About Nvidia's Investigation of Its CEO (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: Apple's software chief Craig Federighi is being pressed to pursue a more ambitious approach to AI as the company aims to transform Siri into an autonomous agent. Federighi has a reputation for being an AI skeptic. His leadership style has sometimes complicated product development and led to delays or less ambitious initial versions of devices, but he has demonstrated an ability to execute when others could not. Siri AI finally fulfills Apple's vision of a working voice assistant, but it is still far from the advanced tools offered by rivals.
items.title: Apple CEO Presses Software Chief to Pursue More Ambitious AI Strategy (17 minute read)

items.summary_html: We are now in an age where longstanding open problems in science and math are dropping like flies. AI is producing proofs at a rate that is hard to keep up with. While many of these proofs have yet to be validated by humans, their Lean certificates provide the confidence needed for their validity. This is causing a stir within the research community.
items.title: Aaronson-Ambainis Conjecture proved! (By AI, of course) (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Amazon has assembled a new team over the past several months to work on a robot product capable of navigating dynamic home environments. The robotics market is expected to surge in the coming years. Amazon redeployed most of the team behind its Astro robot earlier this year and hired an MIT roboticist to work on the new home robot project. It acquired Fauna Robotics, a New York-based startup with a 3.5-foot-tall humanoid robot, in March to create a new division called the Personal Robotics Group.
items.title: Amazon's Astro home robot has fans but looks destined for the ‘trash heap.' Why it's trying again (11 minute read)

items.summary_html: Programming is much more tiring with AI. This is a sign that you are diligently working on things that require human brainpower and judgment. AI is taking over the repetitive and obvious parts of the job, leaving developers to deal with higher-judgment tasks. It is no surprise that these would be more tiring.
items.title: Programming and fatigue (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Large language models don't know how to design software that uses LLMs. This could be because most training code is pre-LLMs, or RLVR may just not be a good environment to write code that calls LLMs. Also, current AI agents might just not be good enough at software design for the task. LLMs are good and bad seemingly at random, but if you can predict where they will do well or badly ahead of time, you can get enormous value from them.
items.title: LLMs are terrible at designing AI systems (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: AI is making it increasingly hard to tell good work from bad work and fakes. Humans rely on shortcuts based on signals to make decisions all the time. AI widely undermines these signals and lowers the incentive to produce good work. The speed and scale of the current signal collapse is unprecedented. We need signals to survive in the modern world, and the rapid collapse of many previously dependable signals will create large shifts in society.
items.title: AI Is Causing Signal Collapse Everywhere All at Once (20 minute read)

items.summary_html: The amount of software being created is going to go up much faster than the number of people paid to make it. AI will enable far more software of a kind nobody used to make. The developer jobs that grow will be the ones that the machines made faster. The demand for software can be bottomless and the work can still move somewhere else.
items.title: The Jevons paradox has a second half (13 minute read)

items.title: Modern CSS Might Make Your Front-End More Complex (22 minute read)
